All three merit measurements were spent in one parallel batch, so the result could not be refined afterwards. No XRD was used.

content.text:
I submitted **index 199** (Cu 0.44, Fe 0.11, V 0.45) as the best composition. Its photocurrent was **17.9 µA**, the highest of the three compositions I measured.

| Index | Composition (Cu / Fe / V) | Target phase | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 199 | 0.44 / 0.11 / 0.45 | β-Cu₂V₂O₇ (1:1 Cu:V) | **17.9 µA** |
| 233 | 0.28 / 0.12 / 0.60 | CuV₂O₆ (1:2 Cu:V) | 15.3 µA |
| 98 | 0.53 / 0.12 / 0.35 | Cu₃V₂O₈ (Cu-rich) | 4.8 µA |

**Mistake:** I spent all 3 merit measurements in one parallel batch. That meant the first results couldn't guide the later picks. With a budget this small, I should have measured one at a time and used the results to narrow the search. A better use of the last one or two measurements would have been a point next to index 199, such as 268 or 260, or a sample of the V-rich area where most of the library sits.

I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements. I also didn't measure anything in the Fe-rich region or the V-rich corner (V above 0.7). So I can't say how close index 199 is to the best composition in the library.
